subject.title: Feature: Opt-in cross-channel visibility in TUI (mirror iMessage/Telegram activity)

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off TUI cross-channel observer or mirror mode, and what transcript visibility boundary should it enforce across agents, sessions, channels, devices, and operators?
rationale: Existing Gateway events make part of the plumbing plausible, but exposing cross-channel transcripts changes privacy, redaction, retention, delivery, CLI/config, and operator-scope policy that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Read-only observer first
options.body: Add an explicit observe mode that shows only authorized activity for the selected agent or session scope and defers bidirectional channel mirroring.

options.title: Full bidirectional mirroring
options.body: Allow TUI and channel messages to appear across surfaces only after delivery, authorization, redaction, and upgrade policy are defined.

options.title: No core mirror mode
options.body: Keep logs, selected-session tailing, or a future activity timeline as the supported monitoring path and avoid cross-channel TUI mirroring in core.

recommendation.title: Read-only observer first
recommendation.body: Add an explicit observe mode that shows only authorized activity for the selected agent or session scope and defers bidirectional channel mirroring.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is tied to the original TUI isolation change and now requires product/security policy for cross-channel transcript visibility.
